head: One giant company.
Thousands of small ones.
slides.sub: How Haier took apart its own hierarchy.

image.label: A huge factory dissolving into many small glowing workshops
image.brief: 거대한 가전 공장 건물이 수많은 작은 불 켜진 작업실로 쪼개지는 초현실적 장면. 위에서 내려다본 구도, 따뜻한 빛. 실제 로고 없음.

head: It started with
a sledgehammer.
body: In 1984, Zhang Ruimin took over a failing refrigerator factory in Qingdao. In a story often told, he had workers smash faulty fridges to show that bad quality would no longer pass.
Over the next two decades, that factory grew into a global appliance maker.

image.label: A sledgehammer resting against a dented 1980s refrigerator
image.brief: 1980년대 중국 공장 바닥, 찌그러진 냉장고 옆에 세워진 망치. 작업복 차림 노동자들의 뒷모습 실루엣. 바랜 필름 톤.

head: Big, global,
and getting slow.
body: By the mid-2000s, Haier had tens of thousands of employees and many layers of managers between the factory floor and the buyer.
The internet was changing what customers expected. Ideas took too long to climb up and down the chain.

image.label: A tall stack of paper approval forms on a desk
image.brief: 2000년대 중국 대기업 사무실, 결재 서류가 높이 쌓인 책상. 뒤로 긴 복도와 닫힌 문들. 차가운 형광등 빛.

head: Your company is huge.
How do you get fast?
body: You lead a successful appliance maker. Profits are fine, but decisions crawl and customers feel far away.

options.text: Break the company into small teams that answer to customers, not bosses
options.feedback: Risky and messy. Thousands of managers lose their old roles, and nobody has a playbook. Keep swiping.

options.text: Keep the hierarchy and add better software and reporting
options.feedback: Safer and easier to sell inside. But faster reports up a tall ladder are still a tall ladder. Keep swiping.

options.text: Hand manufacturing to partners and focus on the brand
options.feedback: Cheaper and lighter. But you give away the factories that made you, and the distance to customers stays. Keep swiping.

image.label: A leader looking at a tall organization chart on a wall
image.brief: 벽에 붙은 거대한 피라미드형 조직도를 바라보는 경영자의 뒷모습 실루엣. 실존 인물 얼굴 없음.

head: Every worker,
facing the customer.
body: In 2005, Zhang announced a model called RenDanHeYi. The idea: link each employee directly to the value they create for users.
Instead of waiting for orders from above, teams would win or lose based on what customers actually bought.

image.label: A worker and a customer separated by nothing but a counter
image.brief: 작업복 입은 직원과 고객이 카운터 하나를 사이에 두고 마주 선 장면. 사이를 막던 벽이 사라진 느낌. 일반적인 인물 실루엣.

slides.label: middle-management roles cut, reportedly, as layers were removed
body: Haier removed whole layers of the company in the 2010s. Some managers left. Others became leaders of small teams that had to earn their own keep.

image.label: Empty manager chairs lined up in a quiet office
image.brief: 텅 빈 관리자 의자들이 줄지어 놓인 조용한 사무실. 창으로 들어오는 아침 햇빛.

head: Small teams,
real stakes.
body: Haier split into thousands of micro-enterprises. Each small team set its own goals, hired its own people and shared in what it earned. Teams that failed could be closed.
One group of young employees, reportedly, studied gamers' online complaints and built a gaming laptop business.

image.label: A small team gathered around a laptop and sketches
image.brief: 작은 팀 몇 명이 노트북과 스케치를 둘러싸고 회의하는 장면. 2010년대 중국 스타트업 분위기. 실제 제품 로고 없음.

slides.label: what Haier paid for GE Appliances in 2016
body: Haier kept the American business largely in local hands and encouraged it to adopt the small-team model over time. The approach was now being tested far beyond China.

image.label: A Midwestern US appliance plant at sunrise
image.brief: 해 뜰 무렵 미국 중서부의 가전 공장 외관. 주차장의 픽업트럭들. 실제 로고나 간판 없음.

head: Still a giant,
but it moves like many.
body: According to the company, citing Euromonitor, Haier has been the world's top major-appliance brand by retail volume year after year since 2009.
The model is hard to copy. It asks people to take real risk, and not every team survives.

image.label: A global map lit with many small points of light
image.brief: 세계 지도 위에 수많은 작은 빛점이 흩어져 반짝이는 그래픽. 하나의 큰 덩어리가 아닌 여러 점.

head: Push decisions down
to where customers are.
body: Big companies usually centralize to stay in control, then lose touch with buyers. Haier went the other way.
Small teams with ownership, clear results and the freedom to act moved faster than any chain of approvals could.

image.label: A pyramid turning upside down into a flat network
image.brief: 피라미드 도형이 뒤집히며 평평한 그물망으로 바뀌는 그래픽. 단순한 선과 강조색.

head: Shorten the distance
to the customer.
body: Every layer between a decision and a customer adds delay. Small teams that own results can close that gap.
**Try it today:** pick one decision your team escalates often. Could the people closest to the customer make it themselves?

image.label: A single small team working late in a bright room
image.brief: 어두운 건물 속 불 켜진 작은 방 하나, 그 안에서 일하는 소수의 팀 실루엣.

factChecks.note: Zhang Ruimin이 1984년 칭다오의 적자 냉장고 공장을 맡은 것과 1985년 불량 냉장고를 망치로 부순 일화는 Haier 공식 연혁 기준입니다. 부순 대수(흔히 76대)는 카드에 넣지 않았고 "a story often told"로 표시했습니다. → [2026-11-02 확인] 1984년 인수, 불량 냉장고 76대 파쇄 일화 확인.
RenDanHeYi(人单合一) 모델 발표 시점(2005년 9월)은 Haier 공식 자료로 확인하세요. → [2026-11-02 확인] RenDanHeYi 2005년 발표는 이번 검색에서 미확인.
중간관리자 약 1만 명 감축은 Hamel·Zanini의 HBR 기사(2018)와 『Humanocracy』(2020) 등에 나오는 수치입니다. 시기와 정의(퇴사인지 역할 전환인지)가 자료마다 달라 "about"과 "reportedly"로 적었습니다.
마이크로 기업 수는 자료마다 수천 개로 다르게 나옵니다(약 2,000~4,000). 카드에는 "thousands"로만 적었습니다. 팀 규모도 "often 10 to 15 people"이 아닌 "small"로만 표현했습니다.
게이밍 노트북 팀(Leishen/ThundeRobot)이 젊은 직원들에 의해 시작되고 온라인 불만 리뷰를 분석해 제품을 만들었다는 내용은 HBR(2018)·『Humanocracy』 보도 기준입니다. 리뷰 건수는 넣지 않았습니다.
2016년 GE Appliances 인수 금액 54억 달러는 당시 GE·Haier 발표와 Reuters 보도로 확인하세요. → [2026-11-02 확인] 2016년 6월 GE Appliances 54억 달러 확인.
Euromonitor 기준 대형 가전 소매 판매량 세계 1위 브랜드(2009년 이후 연속)는 Haier가 발표한 내용이라 "according to the company, citing Euromonitor"로 표시했습니다. → [2026-11-02 확인] 2009년부터 연속 세계 1위(Haier 발표) 확인.

sources.text: Haier Group, company history and materials on the RenDanHeYi model
Hamel, G. & Zanini, M. (2018). The End of Bureaucracy. Harvard Business Review.
Hamel, G. & Zanini, M. (2020). Humanocracy. Harvard Business Review Press.
Reuters coverage of Haier's acquisition of GE Appliances (2016)
